introHeading: Wedding photo booths for Williamsburg's rooftop-to-loft receptions
introParas: A lot of Williamsburg weddings do something most neighborhoods don't ask of us: they move. A rooftop ceremony along Wythe or Kent Avenue gives way to a reception one floor down, or a few blocks over, in a converted loft off Berry Street — sometimes with the wedding party and the booth both making that trip inside the same evening. We plan for that from the start rather than treating a Williamsburg wedding like a single fixed setup, which matters more here than at a traditional catering hall wedding where everything happens in one room.

Guest counts tend to run smaller and younger than the citywide average — Williamsburg weddings we work are usually somewhere between 80 and 150 guests, which keeps a single booth comfortably ahead of the line all night. The mirror booth remains the safest pick for a mixed-age guest list, since the full-length format works from the flower girl to the grandparents; for a couple who wants the reception to look as considered as the invitations, the glam booth's editorial black-and-white portraits are the more requested choice. Either way, if the ceremony is on a rooftop, we plan around wind and a covered position for the equipment the same way we would for any outdoor setup.

On logistics: we carry a $3 million insurance policy and turn a certificate of insurance around the same day you send us your venue's contact, which most Williamsburg rooftop bars and loft venues will ask for before they confirm your date. We arrive an hour ahead and set up in about 20 minutes, in a 10ft x 10ft footprint where the room allows it or 8ft x 8ft with 7.5ft of clearance in a tighter loft. There's no travel fee anywhere in Williamsburg — it's minutes from us, quoted from your venue ZIP code before you book.

faqHeading: Wedding Photo Booth in Williamsburg — FAQ

faqs.q: How many hours should we book for a Williamsburg wedding?
faqs.a: Three to four hours covers most Williamsburg receptions. If your ceremony and reception are in different spots — a rooftop ceremony followed by a loft reception, for instance — tell us the full run sheet so we can plan the booth's move between them.

faqs.q: Does the booth need to move if our ceremony is on a rooftop and the reception is somewhere else?
faqs.a: Yes, and we plan for it. If the reception venue is close enough for the same booth to make both stops, we build the move into your booking; if not, we'll talk through whether two shorter bookings makes more sense.

faqs.q: Which booth works best for a Williamsburg wedding?
faqs.a: The mirror booth is the safest choice for a mixed-age guest list — it's the one most families gather around. For a couple who wants the reception's photos to feel as editorial as the rest of the day, the glam booth's black-and-white portraits are the more requested option, and the look holds through a rooftop's shift from daylight into evening.

faqs.q: Do you charge a travel fee in Williamsburg?
faqs.a: No — Williamsburg is minutes from us. We quote everything from your venue ZIP code before you book.

faqs.q: Our ceremony is on a rooftop — how do you plan for wind and weather?
faqs.a: We treat rooftop weddings the way we'd treat any outdoor equipment setup: a level, wind-sheltered position, secured the same way we'd secure anything tall outdoors, and a conversation with you ahead of time about what happens if the weather turns.

faqs.q: Can the booth get into a Berry Street loft venue through a freight elevator?
faqs.a: Yes. Our booths are built to clear a single freight-elevator trip, the standard load-in for the converted industrial spaces most Williamsburg loft weddings are held in.

faqs.q: Can you send our venue a certificate of insurance?
faqs.a: Yes. We carry a $3 million policy and turn COIs around the same day you send us your venue's contact — most Williamsburg rooftop bars and loft venues ask for one before confirming your date.

faqs.q: Do we get every photo from the night, not just the prints?
faqs.a: Yes. Every image lands in an online gallery you can download in full and share with guests, on top of the unlimited prints handed out on the night.

faqs.q: How much space and power does the booth need?
faqs.a: 10ft x 10ft is optimal, 8ft x 8ft with 7.5ft of ceiling clearance works for a tighter loft floor, plus a standard outlet within 15 feet that isn't shared with the DJ.

faqs.q: What Williamsburg neighborhoods do you cover for weddings?
faqs.a: North Williamsburg, South Williamsburg, East Williamsburg, Wythe Avenue, Berry Street, Kent Avenue and the surrounding areas most weekends of the season. If your venue isn't on that list, ask anyway — we'll tell you honestly whether we can get there.
